XMLDSig signing and validation of Brazilian fiscal XML: NF-e, NFC-e, CT-e, MDF-e (and their events), NFS-e Nacional, eSocial and EFD-Reinf, with ICP-Brasil certificates.

Sign PAdES, CAdES and XAdES documents with cloud certificates: ICP-Brasil PSCs (BirdID, VIDaaS, NeoID, SafeID, RemoteID — ITI API v0, DOC-ICP-17.01) and Cloud Signature Consortium API v2 providers. OAuth 2.0 with PKCE. No third-party dependencies. Native AOT compatible.
XAdES under the ICP-Brasil signature policies: AD-RB, AD-RT, AD-RV, AD-RC and AD-RA signing, policy validation and the verified LPA_XAdES refresh.

Shared building blocks of the SimpleSign Brazilian trust frameworks: CPF/CNPJ, Lei 14.063/2020 levels, the advanced-signature (AEA) manifest and the ITI VALIDAR helpers. Used by SimpleSign.Brazil.IcpBrasil and SimpleSign.Brazil.GovBr.
Gov.br for SimpleSign: bundled Gov.br AC Raiz and intermediates, Gov.br chain validation and assurance level, and the Lei 14.063 advanced level of Gov.br signatures.

ICP-Brasil for SimpleSign: bundled AC Raiz and intermediates, chain validation (DOC-ICP-04), signature policies AD-RB to AD-RA (DOC-ICP-15), standalone ACT timestamps and the Lei 14.063 level of each signature.
Sign PAdES, CAdES and XAdES documents with A3 tokens, smartcards and HSMs through their PKCS#11 driver. Own minimal interop: no third-party dependencies, no unsafe code. Native AOT compatible.
Bartoo.Requestor – client-side runtime to send typed Bartoo requests and await typed replies over any supported broker.
Bartoo – surface client: high-level, broker-agnostic request/reply API over messaging/event-streaming platforms, built on strongly-typed operations and explicit payload contracts.
Bartoo public contracts used by generated stubs and surface integrations (request/reply interfaces, minimal metadata, and stub attributes).
Bartoo.Replier – server-side runtime to host typed handlers and publish typed replies over any supported broker.

Bartoo.Transport.Abstractions – the threshold of the broker: what the runtimes ask of a transport (produce, consume, administer streams) without naming one. An adapter implements it; the boundary never sees the adapter.

Bartoo.ProtocolBinding – the bound operation protocol of the Request–Reply boundary: from the identity of an operation to its request and reply channels, its correlation tokens and the representation of its payloads on the wire.
